top_signals.title: Sahm Warns Fed Against Waiting
top_signals.summary: Former Fed economist Claudia Sahm joins Bloomberg Open Interest to argue the central bank may be taking a bigger risk by waiting to raise rates. She warns persistent inflation could force much larger hikes later, questions the Fed’s mixed messaging to markets and explains why massive AI spending is becoming an increasingly important force for the economy and inflation. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Metals Rally Faces a Reality Check
top_signals.summary: As metals earnings roll in, Wells Fargo Equity Research analyst Timna Tanners sees support for steel prices but urges caution on the copper-AI story. She says AI may account for only a small share of demand, while weakness in China’s property sector remains significant. Aluminum could face new supply, and building materials remain under pressure. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: Odd Lots: The Forgotten Godmother of Economic Literature
top_signals.summary:
Regency-era novelist Maria Edgeworth was famous for including economic concepts into her novels, including the idea of productive labor. Her works were ahead of her time and enormously influential, yet her name is hardly ever mentioned in the history of economics.

On this episode of the Odd Lots podcast, Jeanna Smialek, Brussels bureau chief at The New York Times, tells Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway why she thinks Edgeworth's name needs to be placed back in the pantheon of economic history. (Source: Bloomberg)
